CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  DEVELOPMENT SERVICES DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
December 6, 2023 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to address
  the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other than a
  public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Kelly McDonough,
  representing Verizon Wireless, for Special Use Permit No. SP23-
  00009 to allow the location of a mono-eucalyptus tree wireless
  telecommunication facility and associated equipment in Darby
  Park on an approximately 14-acre, O-S (Open Space) zoned site
  at 3400 West Arbor Vitae Street.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2023-128; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP23-00009 subject to
  25 conditions.
  Item 5a Documents

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Patsy Nguyen, for
  Special Use Permit No. SP23-00018 to allow a nail salon in an
  existing 4,400 square-foot multi-tenant building that is within
  300 feet of a similar use on an approximately 5,600 square-foot,
  C-2(General Commercial) zoned property at 1713-1717 Centinela
  Avenue.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2023-127; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP23-00018 subject
  to 14 conditions.
  Item 5b Documents

  c. A public hearing to consider an application by Michael
  Kimbrough, for Special Use Permit No. SP23-00019 to allow 1) a
  child care facility and 2) building alterations with a valuation
  that exceeds twenty thousand dollars in an existing 10,500
  square-foot commercial building on an approximately 20,200
  square-foot, Residential Medical and Medical Enterprise Overlay
  zoned property at 633 Aerick Street.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2023-126; and
  2)Adopt the attached resolution approving SP23-00019 subject to
  11 conditions.
  Item 5c Documents
 6.  NON-PUBLIC HEARING:
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Legatum
  Holdings, for Design Review No. DR23-00082 to allow the
  construction of a new, 16-story, mixed-use building with
  approximately 4,500 square feet of retail floor area, 162
  apartment units, and associated parking on an approximately
  20,000 square-foot MU-1(Mixed Use-1)zoned property at 330 East
  Florence Avenue.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2022-139; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR23-00082 subject to
  8 conditions.
  Item 6a Documents

7.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning Commission
  on any matter within their j urisdiction and not elsewhere
  considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

8.  Commission Initiatives.

9.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability, please
contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One Manchester
Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All
requests for special accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to
the day of the hearing(s).

"Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de
llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of December 6, 2023,
is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda
item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda
item will automatically be continued to the next regular Planning
Commission meeting.

  ONE MANCHESTER BOULEVARD
  INGLEWOOD, CA 90301

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, December 6, 2023, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Carolyn Fowler
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, DSD Director
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Cynthia Robinson, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. McCrumby, Senior Planner stated 1) Item 5C. - Staff received
ten letters of support. 2) Item 6A. - The environmental
determination categorical exemption was changed, and copies were
provided for the Commissioners and updated on the city’s website.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
Larisse Barksdale – Local business owner in support of Item 6A.
Patricia Franklin – Supports Item 6A.
Jessica Cabala – Supports Item 6A.
Lizz Lynn – Resident in support of Item 6A
Allison Harrison – Resident looking forward to the beautification
of Market Street.

(5) PUBLIC HEARINGS:
5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. (SP-23-00009): A public hearing to
consider an application by Kelly McDonough, representing Verizon
Wireless, for Special Use Permit No. SP23-00009 to allow the
location of a mono-eucalyptus tree wireless telecommunication
facility and associated equipment in Darby Park on an approximately
14-acre, O-S (Open Space) zoned site at 3400 West Arbor Vitae
Street.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the Staff Presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler commented that this additional service is
needed.

Commissioner Rice asked staff -
 Does anything beyond 40 feet in height require a Zone Variance
  Approval?
 Why was that level picked for Zone Variance Approval?
   Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 6, 2023

Commissioner Trejo commented that she appreciated  the  25
recommended conditions to help camouflage the tower.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated that she also likes that the
tower is camouflaged.

Christopher Jackson stated that he wanted to add that the
applicant has already filed for a variance and it is being
considered by staff.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 Are the trees that surround the antenna taller or shorter than
  the antenna?
   Mr. Salazar responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs invited the applicant to come  before  the
Planning Commission to speak about the project.

Justin Robinson, representing Verizon addressed the Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Hearing none, Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the
audience to speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
1. Andre Cheeks – Inglewood Resident – Against this project.
2. Jacqueline Cheeks – Inglewood Resident – Against this project.
3. Marsha Johnson – Inglewood Business Owner – Against this
  project.

Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney stated that there is no
evidence that the facilities are not in compliance with FCC
regulations, so this is not something that the Commission would
consider.

Chairman Springs stated it is their job as Commissioners to listen
to what their residents are saying so they can make an appropriate
decision for this particular antenna.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant -
 Would the height of the antenna affect the aircraft?
   Mr. Jackson stated that Mr. Pan was letting the commission
  know that their decision cannot be based on radio emissions
  and health.
 Has Verizon gone to the Federal Government to get their
  approval?
   Ms. Janelle Hartley, representing Verizon, stated that
  Verizon is compliant with FCC regulations.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Did you talk to the residents to let them know that you were
  putting the monopole there?
  - Ms. Hartley answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo stated that Verizon has done a great job as
far as providing something that is necessary.

Commissioner Fowler stated that she does not see a reason not to
approve this at this moment.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 6, 2023
Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made a motion to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2023-128; and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-23-00009 subject to 25 conditions and it was
seconded by Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1976.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO KELLY
  MCDONOUGH, REPRESENTING VERIZON WIRELESS TO
  ALLOW THE LOCATION OF A MONO-EUCALYPTUS TREE
  WIRELESS  TELECOMMUNICATION  FACILITY  AND
  ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT IN DARBY PARK ON AN
  APPROXIMATELY 14-ACRE O-S (OPEN SPACE) ZONED
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 3400 WEST ARBOR VITAE
  STREET.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fowler, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.

Mr. McCrumby explained the appeal process.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 23-00018 (SP-23-00018):
A public hearing to consider an application by Patsy Nguyen, for
Special Use Permit No. SP23-00018 to allow a nail salon in an
existing 4,400 square-foot multi-tenant building that is within
300 feet of a similar use on an approximately 5,600 square-foot,
C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 1713-1717 Centinela
Avenue.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
 What is the nearest residential area?
   Mr.  Leon-Martell  responded  to  Commissioner  Fowler’s
  question.

Chairman Springs asked the Applicant to come before the Planning
Commission to speak about the project.

Tuan Tran, representing the nail salon addressed the Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Trejo stated she is glad that staff differentiated
the type of services provided by the existing cosmetology use and
the applicant.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated she is glad that they take a
day off and close on Wednesdays.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 6, 2023

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to

Hearing none, Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and

Hearing none, Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Fowler made a motion to affirm categorical exemption

Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1977.

  (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT
  1713-1717 CENTINELA AVENUE.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fowler, Rice, Shaw-Williams, Trejo and
  Chairman Springs.

Mr. McCrumby explained the appeal process.

5C. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 23-00019 (SP-23-00019):
A public hearing to consider an application by Michael Kimbrough
for Special Use Permit No. SP23-00019 to allow 1) a child care
facility and 2) building alterations with a valuation that
exceeds twenty thousand dollars in an existing 10,500 square-foot
commercial building on an approximately 20,200 square-foot,
Residential Medical and Medical Enterprise Overlay zoned property
at 633 Aerick Street.

Mr. McCrumby stated that ten letters of support were provided for
this item.

Ms. Christine Rivera, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Were the letters of support from parents of the Los Angeles
  site?
 Will this site be run similarly to the way the Los Angeles
  site is being run?
   Ms. Rivera responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 The west side of the parking lot will be open for the play
  area when cars are not there?
   Ms. Rivera responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
December 6, 2023
Chairman Springs invited the applicant to come  before  the
Planning Commission to speak about the project.

Michael Kimbrough,  Project  Manager  addressed  the  Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
 How will the project benefit the community?
 Is this a preschool?
 What are you prepared to do to ensure the safety of the drop-
  off and pickup?
 What additional eyes are there to provide safety during drop-
  off and pickup?
 Will there be security cameras?
  - Ms. Britany Crawford and Mr. Kimbrough responded to
  Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 How do the locked doors operate?
   Mr. Kimbrough responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 What is the CPR training requirement and how often do the staff
  need to be recertified?
   Ms. Crawford responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams
  question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
 Is there an alarm system on the doors that would notify the
  police and fire department in an emergency?
 Is there a time mechanism on the door that once the door is
  open for any length of time the door will automatically close?
 Where is the school located that you are operating right now?
   Ms. Crawford & Mr. Kimbrough responded to Chairman Springs’
  questions.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

Seeing none, Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and
called for final comments from the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
 Will there be support in terms of emergency health?
  - Ms. Crawford responded to Commissioner Fowler’s question.

Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made a motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2023-126; and adopt the attached resolution approving SP-
23-00019 subject to 11 conditions and an additional condition to
read that all access doors to the facility shall remain locked,
that its panic hardware be maintained to be in working order and
at no time shall the doors be propped open and if exiting from
the doors that they be supervised by more than one person. It was
seconded by Commissioner Rice, that Resolution No. 1978

  5

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:
6A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 23-00082 (DR-23-00082)330 EAST FLORENCE
AVENUE:
A non-public hearing to consider an application by Legatum
Holdings, for Design Review No. DR23-00082 to allow the
construction of a new, 16-story, mixed-use building with
approximately 4,500 square feet of retail floor area, 162
apartment units, and associated parking on an approximately
20,000 square-foot MU-1 (Mixed Use-1) zoned property at 330 East
Florence Avenue.

Mr. Salazar, Planner stated there are two corrections to the
Staff report. He stated that on page two, the second sentence
should read ten lots instead of four. He also stated that under
site design section the street frontages should read one hundred
seventy-four feet not one hundred and forty-one feet.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the Staff Presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
 Will there be a heliport?
 Where will it be located?
  - Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Is the pedestrian ingress and egress on Locust and Florence,
  but the one-way driveways in and out are just on Locust?
 Is there a security gate that prevents pedestrians from walking
  in off the street?
  - Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Is there retail?
 It has a twenty percent affordable unit component?
  -Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Trejo commented that this project will make this
part of Market Street a lovely promenade.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff –
 How many penthouse units and what is the square footage?
   Mr.  Salazar  responded  to  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams’

Chairman Springs asked the Applicant to come before the Planning

Mr. William Lowery, representing Legatum Holdings addressed the

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any

Commissioner Rice stated that this  was  probably  the  best
